title: Hosted API graceful-degrade: per-tenant retry quarantine and short-circuit hotpatch
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported spikes of 5xx and tail latency increases during heavy tenant traffic windows. Investigation shows a cascade: aggressive client retries + proxy fanout + KV-cache churn created transient request amplification and head-of-line blocking, causing backend worker saturation and 5xx responses.

Root cause hypotheses and evidence:
- Retry amplification: clients retried idempotent and non-idempotent requests during timeouts; upstream proxy had no tenant-scoped inflight caps, causing one noisy tenant to monopolize GPU workers. (traces: https://datadog.example/org/redwood/trace/shotgun)
- KV cache eviction shift: bursts changed typical sequence-length distribution, forcing large KV cache writes during sharded inference hot path and causing GC/compaction stalls on the runtime host. (metrics: KVCache.evictions_per_minute spike on 2026-03-03 14:12 UTC)
- Proxy batching interaction: continuous batching combined with concurrent hedging produced worker starvation when batch sizes exceeded kernel-optimized assumptions.

Immediate mitigations implemented (hotpatches):
1) Deploy proxy config patch to enforce tenant-level concurrent_inflight=limit (default 8) and per-connection keepalive reductions. Rollout: staged to 20% region traffic (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/7891).
2) Add short-circuit responder for known idempotent endpoints: if request contains idempotency-key and tenant is in degraded state, return 429 with Retry-After header (temporary to force client backoff).
3) Enabled emergency KVCache compaction throttle to smooth compaction work.

Planned longer-term fixes:
- Retry Quarantine subsystem: per-tenant adaptive quarantine that progressively reduces allowed concurrency and hedging multipliers when backend error rate or worker saturation crosses thresholds. Design doc: https://confluence.example/redwood/retry-quarantine
- Workload-aware kernel selection fallback: ensure runtime selects smaller-batch kernels during tenant surges to preserve predictability.
- SDK guidance & default client-timeout harmonization: coordinate SDK timeouts and retry defaults to avoid amplification.

Reproduction steps for SRE/ENG:
1) Use the tenant-surge-sim harness (tools/tenant-surge) with a mix of long-sequence and short-sequence requests, and client retry=3 at 200ms backoff.
2) Observe KVCache eviction and proxy inflight counts; reproduce 5xx wave.

Acceptance criteria / Done when:
- Hotpatch is rolled to all regions and reduces customer-visible 5xx by >90% during simulated surges.
- Retry Quarantine PoC merged and e2e tested on staging with no regression to latency p50.
- Postmortem and customer communication drafted and sent to impacted customer list.

Artifacts and links:
- Hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/7891
- Runtime throttle PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2210
- Runbook: https://confluence.example/redwood/hosted-api-5xx-runbook
- Incident dashboard: https://grafana.example/d/hosted-api/tenant-surge
